private_note: One draw, a generation long: I weigh the bottom heavily but won't give up a fifth of average income for it. Alder has Today's average with a higher floor (32 vs 22), so it beats Today for anyone who dislikes risk. Under log utility Alder > Today > Cedar > Hazel > Birch. Cedar's 15 floor is too dangerous for its extra mean. Hazel and Birch cost too much at the middle and top. Alder is also the likeliest point to reach 9 votes.
statement: Fellow delegates, none of us knows which fifth we will draw, and whatever we choose lasts a generation. Look at Alder next to Today. The average is the same, 100. The lowest fifth rises from 22 to 32 and the second fifth gains a little. The fourth and top fifths give up only 2 and 10. Anyone who would rather not gamble should take that trade. Cedar raises the average, but it does so by risking a one-in-five chance at 15 with no health coverage. Hazel and Birch protect the bottom, but they cut the average by a fifth, and most of us would pay for that in the middle and upper groups. Alder is the plan that every careful delegate can accept, wherever their own appetite for risk lies, and it needs nine of us. I'm asking you to rank Alder first so we leave here with an agreement instead of a failed convention.
